Calculate Stress for a fitted rrGDM model

Source: R/stress.R
stress.Rd

Computes a goodness-of-fit "stress" statistic for a fitted rrGDM object, comparing the observed dissimilarities used to fit the model against a model-implied quantity computed from the conditional latent coordinates (i.e., including sample-level errors): either the raw Euclidean distance between fitted latent positions (scale = "link"), or the inverse-link-transformed expected dissimilarity (scale = "response").

For type = "nonmetric", this is Kruskal's stress-1, $$Stress = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (\hat{d} - D)^2}{\sum D^2}}$$ where \(D\) is the chosen model-implied quantity and \(\hat{d}\) ("disparities") is the isotonic (monotone) regression of \(D\) on the observed dissimilarities.

For type = "metric", observed and model-implied dissimilarities are compared directly, with no regression step: $$Stress = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (y_{ij} - \hat{y}_{ij})^2}{\sum y_{ij}^2}}$$ where \(y_{ij}\) are the observed dissimilarities and \(\hat{y}_{ij}\) the model-implied ones. Because it does not allow for a linear recalibration, it also penalises a poorly calibrated link. This is not directly comparable to the stress reported by NMDS software.

Stress is returned as a proportion between 0 (best) and 1 (worst) for bounded dissimilarities.

Usage

stress(object, type = c("nonmetric", "metric"), scale = c("link", "response"))

Arguments

object

A fitted object of class rrGDM.

type

Character string: "nonmetric" (default) computes Kruskal's stress-1 using isotonic regression, as in standard NMDS. "metric" compares observed and model-implied dissimilarities directly (see Description).

scale

Character string: "link" (default) uses the raw Euclidean distance between fitted latent positions in the ordination. This is generally the only scale on which stress values from RRGDM and other methods (e.g., vegan::metaMDS, MASS::isoMDS) should be compared directly. "response" instead uses the inverse-link transformed expected dissimilarity (object$inv_link(dist)), which is on the same scale as the observed dissimilarities used to fit the model. This is the appropriate scale for type = "metric".

Value

A single numeric value: the stress.

Examples

set.seed(2)
# simulate data
n <- 25 # sites
p <- 25 # species

env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n))
eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)
Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p,
            dimnames = list(paste0("site", 1:n), paste0("sp", 1:p)))

fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,
             formula = ~ temp + moist,
             family = "binomial")
#> ℹ Preparing data
#> ✔ Preparing data ... done
#> 
#> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA)
#> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done
#> 
#> ℹ optimisation
#> ℹ Start 1/1: objective = 1670.1661
#> ℹ optimisation

#> ✔ optimisation ... done
#> 

stress(fit)
#> [1] 0.09938138
stress(fit, type = "metric", scale = "response")
#> [1] 0.06024978
